## TL;DR

RepoOS can now drive Muse Code (`muse` 1.4.x) as an engineer, reviewer, or PM harness. The driver speaks `muse exec --json`, mints a UUID session id and resends trust and approval flags on every turn, records token usage without inventing a cost, and leaves official certification to #1039 (`verifiedAt` stays null).

## Work and rationale

The adapter follows the same contract as Crush and OpenCode, with three Muse-specific constraints confirmed against the JSON schema and small live runs (spark model, three model steps, throwaway directories, sandbox left on).

The stream is one MSP envelope per line: `stream`, `payload_type`, and `payload`. The session id is the envelope's stream id. Muse rejects anything that is not a UUID (exit 2), so RepoOS generates a random UUID per conversation instead of the `repoos-<task>-<role>` string other drivers use. A second `exec --session-id` with that UUID returns the same stream id, which is how resume is proven. There is no `--continue` flag in this driver.

Trust and approval are not remembered between processes. Every launch sends `--trust-workspace`, `--approval-mode never` (sandbox on, never `--yolo`), `--max-model-steps`, and the configured `--model`. Advisory turns add `--disable-write` and `--disable-shell`. Live checks showed a write attempt refused and no file created. The tradeoff is explicit: a Muse PM cannot run the `repoos` CLI itself, and a Muse reviewer cannot run `git diff` or tests. File reads still work, and RepoOS applies output through its own patch path.

Cancellation uses the default SIGTERM. A live long run stopped promptly and left no orphaned children, so the contract does not switch to Crush's SIGINT.

Usage comes from the terminal `run.usage` record (`input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cached_tokens`, `calls`). Even a one-word prompt reports tens of thousands of input tokens because Muse sends its own system prompt and tool definitions. There is no cost field, so the Tokens tab shows tokens with cost unknown. Tool cards use `task.lifecycle.side_effect_intent` closed by `tool.result`. Tool arguments are not on the stream, so cards show name and output only.

There is no `muse models` subcommand. Discovery is `muse model-profile show <model>` plus a fixed list: default `muse-spark-1.3`, with `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` listed for contributor-mode runs. `--reasoning-effort` exists on the CLI, but RepoOS has no per-task reasoning path, so runs keep the CLI default.

Detection treats Muse like Crush: drivable, install hint, auth hint, and no machine-readable auth probe. The Agents view labels the CLI "Muse Code". The compatibility manifest and the user-docs table mark the release Pending. `CONTRACT_TEMPLATES`, fixture tests, and a credential-free fake binary cover argument shape, UUID minting, read-only flags, event parsing, and usage extraction.

## Approaches tried

Copying the pi session-id shape was the first fit and the wrong one. A live `exec` with a non-UUID id exited 2, so the driver mints UUIDs and tests reject any other shape.

`--yolo` would have skipped the sandbox. The task forbids it. `--approval-mode never` keeps the sandbox and still runs headless.

A `muse models` discovery command does not exist. Pinning a fixed list plus `model-profile show` matches the binary without a network catalog.

SIGTERM was measured before changing the contract template. It reaped the run, so the Crush SIGINT special case was not copied.

## Challenges and blockers

Earlier turns treated a red `repoos check` as a blocker owned by this branch. The failing assertion was a pre-existing mismatch between `AGENTS.md` pressure-guard wording and `default-agent-prompts.test.ts` on main, tracked as #1041. Restoring the wording the test asserts made the scoped gate about this diff again.

Handoff then failed in UI verification: the automatic browser capture of the Agents view timed out. The only UI edit is the "Muse Code" label in the CLI map. This turn declares one shot of `/agents?tab=default` highlighting `.agents-page-title` so capture has a single stable target instead of an open-ended page walk.

Live runs stayed inside the authorized budget (spark, three steps, temp dirs, no credentials in the repo). They answer driver questions only. Certification remains #1039.

## Key learnings

Muse's stream id is the session. If the id you pass is not a UUID, the process never starts. Options are process-local: resume must repeat `--trust-workspace` and `--approval-mode never` or the worktree loads untrusted and AGENTS.md is skipped. Token counts are real and large; cost is absent, and the sessions table should record that absence rather than estimate a dollar figure. Advisory read-only flags are effective, and they also mean Muse cannot be the process that shells out to RepoOS.
